title: Praise and Exaltation
overview: Psalm 113 is a jubilant call to praise the LORD, emphasizing His exalted position above all nations and His compassionate care for the lowly. This short psalm celebrates God's eternal name and His universal reign, highlighting His humility in caring for the needy and His power to uplift the poor and barren. It serves as a reminder of God's sovereign majesty and intimate involvement in human affairs, encouraging believers to worship Him continually. Positioned within the Hallel Psalms, it reflects the joyful worship tradition of Israel and points forward to the messianic hope of restoration and blessing.
structure:
**Verses 1-3: The Call to Praise.** The psalm opens with a universal summons for the servants of the LORD to praise His name continually, from sunrise to sunset, establishing praise as a perpetual duty.

**Verses 4-6: The Exalted Majesty of God.** These verses declare God's supreme position above all nations and the heavens, yet also His humility in observing the affairs of earth, highlighting the paradox of divine transcendence and immanence.

**Verses 7-9: God's Compassion and Deliverance.** The psalm concludes by illustrating God's power to raise the poor and needy from lowly conditions to positions of honor, and to bless the barren woman with children, underscoring His gracious intervention in human need and His cause for joyful praise.

keyVerses.text: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised.
keyVerses.significance: This verse emphasizes the continual nature of worship, affirming that God's name deserves praise at all times and places, reflecting His eternal and unchanging glory.

keyVerses.text: The LORD is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens.
keyVerses.significance: This verse proclaims God's supreme sovereignty over all peoples and creation, affirming His unmatched majesty and divine authority.

keyVerses.text: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth the needy out of the dunghill;
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights God's compassionate intervention on behalf of the lowly, demonstrating His power to elevate and restore those in humble circumstances.

keyVerses.text: He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the LORD.
keyVerses.significance: This verse illustrates God's blessing in bringing life and joy where there was barrenness, symbolizing His ability to bring hope and fulfillment, culminating in a call to praise.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: The sovereign God exalted above all nations and the heavens, who humbles Himself to care for the lowly and needy. He is the central figure acting with both majesty and mercy in this psalm.

characters.name: Servants of the LORD
characters.description: The worshippers called to praise God's name continually. They represent the faithful community who respond to God's exalted nature and gracious acts with joyful praise.

themes.description: Psalm 113 emphasizes God's supreme position above all creation and nations, reinforcing the biblical theme of God's unparalleled sovereignty and glory.

The psalm highlights God's care for the poor, needy, and barren, showing His willingness to uplift and bless those in humble circumstances, consistent with the biblical narrative of God's justice and mercy.

The call to praise from sunrise to sunset underscores the believer's ongoing responsibility to worship God, reflecting the biblical emphasis on continual devotion and acknowledgment of God's holiness.

historicalContext: Psalm 113 is part of the Hallel Psalms (Psalms 113-118), traditionally sung during Jewish festivals such as Passover. Composed likely during or after the exile period, it reflects the restored community's renewed emphasis on praising God's sovereignty and mercy. The geographic setting is ancient Israel, where worship was central to communal identity, and praising God was both a religious and social act. Politically, Israel had experienced foreign domination, making the affirmation of God's exalted status above all nations particularly poignant. The imagery of raising the poor and barren would resonate deeply in a society familiar with hardship and divine deliverance.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God's sovereign majesty and providential care as seen in this psalm, interpreting the lifting of the lowly as a demonstration of God's grace and election, encouraging believers to respond with continual praise.

Dispensationalists often see Psalm 113 as prophetic, pointing to the future messianic kingdom where God will exalt the humble and bless the barren, aligning with promises of restoration and blessing in the millennial reign.

Early church interpreters viewed this psalm typologically, seeing God's lifting of the poor as a foreshadowing of Christ's incarnation and exaltation, and the barren woman as a symbol of the Church receiving spiritual fruitfulness.

crossReferences.connection: Mary’s song echoes Psalm 113’s theme of God exalting the humble and bringing down the mighty.
James affirms God’s choice of the poor to be rich in faith, reflecting the psalm’s emphasis on God lifting the needy.
The call to arise and shine parallels the psalm’s call to praise from sunrise to sunset, highlighting God’s glory among nations.
Paul quotes the psalms to show God’s name being praised among the Gentiles, connecting to Psalm 113’s universal call to worship.
Hannah’s prayer shares themes of God’s exaltation of the humble and blessing the barren, closely related to Psalm 113.

application: Commit to praising God throughout your daily routine, recognizing His eternal worthiness.
Trust in God’s sovereign power to uplift you in times of hardship and need.
Celebrate God’s blessings in your life, especially His provision in areas of barrenness or lack.
Encourage others by sharing testimonies of God’s compassionate intervention.
Cultivate humility by remembering God’s care for the lowly and needy.
Engage in corporate worship with a heart of continual praise, joining the community of believers.
conclusion: Psalm 113 stands as a timeless anthem of praise, reminding believers of God’s unmatched majesty and tender compassion. It calls the faithful to worship God continually, recognizing His sovereign reign over all nations and His gracious care for the lowly. This psalm encourages believers to trust in God’s power to transform lives and circumstances, inspiring joyful praise that flows from both awe and gratitude. Its enduring message challenges Christians today to live in humble dependence on God while boldly proclaiming His glory.

definitions.definition: To be endowed with divine favor and happiness; often used to express praise and gratitude toward God.
A heap or pile of manure or refuse; symbolizing lowliness and degradation in biblical imagery.
Unable to bear children; often used metaphorically for spiritual or physical barrenness that God can reverse.
Those who are devoted to serving God, often referring to the faithful community or worshippers.

outline.heading: Call to Praise the LORD
outline.description: An invitation to God's servants to praise His name continually, emphasizing the eternal and universal nature of worship.

outline.heading: God’s Exalted Position
outline.description: Declaration of God's supreme sovereignty above all nations and heavens, coupled with His humility in observing creation.

outline.heading: God’s Compassionate Intervention
